AutogenCommandLine — User Manual

1. Overview

AutogenCommandLine.exe is a console (non-GUI) automation tool for Teradyne IGXL test-program generation and validation. It is a single executable that hosts several sub-tools ("entries"): full test-program autogeneration, test-plan validation, bincut/efuse script checking, character-based autogen (C-Autogen), an AI-assisted autogen path, and TagDiff. Each entry is selected on the command line with -e <EntryName>; there is no window to launch or click through, so this manual documents the CLI surface and the files each entry reads/produces.

2. Command Dispatch Model

Every invocation follows the same pipeline, implemented in CommandLineManager.ParseArgList / CommandLineManager.Execute:

ParseRead -e / --entry and the raw argument list
➜
Select Options maps the entry to a typed options class
➜
Select App maps the entry to its handler
➜
ValidateValidateInput checks required files/folders exist
➜
ExecuteHandler runs; NLog log file is written and copied to the output folder

The process exit code comes from GenerateIgxlMain.ReturnValue (0 = success, 1 = an exception or a reported failure occurred during execution).

Entry Types

Entry (-e value)Options classHandlerPurpose
Autogen (default)AutogenOptionsAutogenCommandLineAppGenerates a full IGXL test program from a test-plan workbook plus SCGH/bincut/voltage/pattern inputs.
ValidationAutogenOptionsValidationCommandLineAppValidates the same inputs as Autogen without generating a program; writes an error report.
BinCutCheck / BinCutEFuseCheck / EFuseCheckCheckScriptOptionsCheckScriptCommandLineAppPost-silicon check: verifies bincut and/or efuse behavior against a datalog.
CAutogenCharAutogenOptionsCAutogenCommandLineAppCharacter-plan-driven ("C-Autogen") pattern/instance generation from a base test program.
CPreCheckerCharAutogenOptionsPreCheckerCommandLineAppSame inputs as CAutogen, but runs in check-only mode (LocalSpecs.CheckOnly = true) without writing a program.
AutoAIAiAutogenOptionsAutoAiCommandLineAppAI-assisted autogen path; loads the char plan / base test program context and hands off to the AI generation pipeline.
TagDiffTagDiffOptionsTagDiffCommandLineAppCompares an autogen test program to a production reference sheet-by-sheet and writes an automation-rate Excel report. (Folds in the former standalone TagDiffCli.exe.)
BenchLogBenchLogOptionsnot yet wiredOptions class exists in MyCommandLineLib.Options, but CommandLineFactory.GetSubCommandLineApplication has no dedicated branch for it, so it currently falls through to the generic AutogenCommandLineApp handler. See BenchLog.

Global Flags

FlagEffect
-e, --entry <name>Selects the entry (see table above). If omitted, the tool defaults to the Autogen options/handler.
-? or bare ?Prints help and exits (only Autogen/Validation have entry-specific help text; other entries fall back to the Autogen help).
-rPrints the tool version and a short changelog, then exits.
-m, --mock 1Enables mock mode: freezes the clock to a fixed date, mocks the assembly-version provider, and marks the run as a unit test (deterministic file names/paths). Present on every entry.
Argument parsing is case-insensitive and unknown arguments are ignored (CaseSensitive = false, IgnoreUnknownArguments = true in CommandLineManager), so passing extra flags for an entry you are not using is harmless.

3. End-to-End Test Workflow

A typical validation loop chains three separate invocations together through the files each step produces: a test plan becomes a test program, the test program is run on the tester to produce a datalog, and the datalog is checked against the program. See CLI Usage below for the full flag reference for each entry used here.

Test Plan
➜
Validation-e Validation checks the test plan for input errors (optional)
➜
Autogen-e Autogen generates the IGXL test program
➜
TagDiff-e TagDiff confirms automation rate against a production reference (optional)
➜
Test Program.igxl program, run on the tester (outside this tool)
➜
Data LogDatalog produced by that tester run
➜
CheckScript-e BinCutCheck / EFuseCheck checks the datalog

Optionally run -e Validation against the test plan before -e Autogen to catch input errors early, and run -e TagDiff against the generated test program to confirm its automation rate before sending it to the tester. 

REM 1. (optional) validate the test plan first
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e Validation -t "TestPlan.xlsx" -o "Validaton_ErrorReport.xlsx" -m 1

REM 2. generate the test program from the test plan
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e Autogen -p Delos -t "TestPlan.xlsx" -o "Validaton_ErrorReport.xlsx" ^
  -d "C:\VBT" --repo "C:\Repo" --job CP1 --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  --needsheet "NeedSheetConfig_Default.xml" --compilePat "compiled.csv" --eqn "EQN.xlsx" -m 1

REM 3. (optional) confirm automation rate against a production reference
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e TagDiff -a "Output\Program.igxl" -p "UR89_CP1_PROD.igxl" -o "Output" --job CP1

REM 4. run the generated program on the tester (outside this tool) to produce a datalog

REM 5. check the datalog against the program
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e BinCutEFuseCheck -f "input\datalog" -p "Output\Program.igxl" ^
  -b "EFUSE_BitDef_Table.txt" -c "Config_table.txt" -o "output"

C-Autogen

The character-plan-driven path starts from an existing base test program instead of a test plan. Optionally run -e CPreChecker against the char plan first to catch input errors early, then run -e CAutogen to generate the updated test program, and finally run -e TagDiff to confirm its automation rate against a production reference before sending it to the tester.

Base Test ProgramExisting .igxl program plus a char plan
➜
CPreChecker-e CPreChecker checks the char plan for input errors (optional)
➜
CAutogen-e CAutogen generates the updated IGXL test program
➜
TagDiff-e TagDiff confirms automation rate against a production reference
REM 1. (optional) check the char plan first
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e CPreChecker -p Delos -a "PatternFolder" --job CP1 --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  --charplan "CharPlan.xlsx" -g "PatternInfo.txt" -c "PatternList.csv" -o "Output" -b "Base.igxl" --cslibrarypath "C:\Library\bin" -m 1

REM 2. generate the updated test program from the char plan
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e CAutogen -p Delos -a "PatternFolder" --job CP1 --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  --charplan "CharPlan.xlsx" -g "PatternInfo.txt" -c "PatternList.csv" -o "Output" -b "Base.igxl" --cslibrarypath "C:\Library\bin" -m 1

REM 3. confirm automation rate against the production reference
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e TagDiff -a "Output\Program.igxl" -p "UR89_CP1_PROD.igxl" -o "Output" --job CP1

AutoAI

The AI-assisted path stages the same job/pattern/channelmap/char-plan/library context as Autogen, but today it does not call into any generation engine — running -e AutoAI stages that context and returns without producing a test program.

Base Test ProgramExisting .igxl program plus a char plan
➜
AutoAI-e AutoAI stages context only — no test program is produced today
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e AutoAI -p Delos -a "PatternFolder" --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  -b "Base.igxl" --cslibrarypath "C:\Library\bin" -o "Output" --job CP1 --charplan "CharPlan.xlsx"

4. CLI Usage

Autogen

Generates a complete IGXL test program. This is the default entry and has the largest option surface.

AutogenCommandLine.exe -e Autogen -p Delos -t "TestPlan.xlsx" -o "Validaton_ErrorReport.xlsx" ^
  -d "C:\VBT" --repo "C:\Repo" --job CP1 --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  --needsheet "NeedSheetConfig_Default.xml" --compilePat "compiled.csv" --eqn "EQN.xlsx" -m 1

How to Use

➜
Run CommandCall with -e Autogen and the required flags below
➜
Check OutputOpen the generated IGXL program; review Error.txt
➜
Fix & RerunIf errors are reported, correct inputs and rerun

Validation

Runs the same test-plan/config resolution as Autogen but performs validation checks instead of generating a program; any errors are appended to Error.txt next to the output file. It reuses AutogenOptions, so the flags above apply, though only the following are actually enforced: test plan, SCGH, pattern-list CSV, bincut, post-bincut, bincut-mode-sequence, voltage table, pattern-info, OTP, YAML, pattern/timeset/bas folders, output file. 

AutogenCommandLine.exe -e Validation -t "TestPlan.xlsx" -o "Validaton_ErrorReport.xlsx" -m 1

How to Use

Prepare InputsSame test plan/config files you plan to run through Autogen
➜
Run CommandCall with -e Validation before committing to a full Autogen run
➜
Check OutputReview Error.txt next to the output file for validation errors
➜
Fix & RerunOnce clean, proceed to -e Autogen with the same inputs

BinCutCheck / BinCutEFuseCheck / EFuseCheck

Post-silicon script checker. -e selects which checks run against a datalog: BinCutCheck runs only the bincut check, EFuseCheck runs only the efuse check, and BinCutEFuseCheck runs both (the handler classifies the entry string case-insensitively for "BinCut"/"EFUSE"/"ALL"). 

REM BinCut check
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e BincutCheck -f "input\datalog" -p "XXX.igxl" -o "output"

REM EFuse check
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e EFuseCheck -f "input\datalog" -b "EFUSE_BitDef_Table.txt" -c "Config_table.txt" -o "output"

How to Use

Prepare InputsDatalog plus program/config/bitdef files for the check(s) you need
➜
Run CommandPick -e BinCutCheck, EFuseCheck, or BinCutEFuseCheck
➜
Check OutputReview the pass/fail results written to the output folder
FlagRequiredDescription
-f, --logfolderYesData log file/folder.
-eNoCheck type: BinCut, EFUSE, VALIDATION, or ALL.
-p, --programNoInput test program.
-c, --configNoEfuse config input file.
-b, --bitdefNoEfuse bit-def table input file.
-o, --otpfilesfolderNoOutput files folder.

CAutogen / CPreChecker

Both entries share CharAutogenOptions. CAutogen runs the full character-plan-driven generation; CPreChecker runs the same setup in check-only mode (no output test program is written, just validation). 

AutogenCommandLine.exe -e CAutogen -p Delos -a "PatternFolder" --job CP1 --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  --charplan "CharPlan.xlsx" -g "PatternInfo.txt" -c "PatternList.csv" -o "Output" -b "Base.igxl" --cslibrarypath "C:\Library\bin" -m 1

How to Use

Prepare InputsBase test program, pattern folder, char plan, pattern list/info files
➜
Run CommandUse -e CPreChecker first to validate, then -e CAutogen to generate
➜
Check OutputCAutogen: open the generated program; CPreChecker: review the report only
FlagRequiredDescription
-p, --currentprojectYesCurrent project name.
-a, --patternfolderYesPattern folder.
--jobYesJob name.
--channelmapYesChannel map name.
--charplanYesChar plan file.
-g, --patterninfofileYesPattern info file.
-c, --patlistcsvfileYesPattern list CSV file.
-o, --outputfolderYesOutput folder.
-b, --basetestprogramYesBase test program to start from.
--cslibrarypathYesC# library path (implies the default C# VBT bas folder).
-n, --genpatnotuseNoSwitch flag.
-r, --gencharnotuseNoSwitch flag.
-m, --mockNo0/1 — mock mode.

AutoAI

AI-assisted autogen path; sets up pattern/library context and hands off to the AI generation pipeline.

This entry only stages job/pattern/channelmap/char-plan/library configuration and returns; it does not call into any generation engine. Today this entry only stages context — it does not itself run an AI generation pipeline. 
AutogenCommandLine.exe -e AutoAI -p Delos -a "PatternFolder" --channelmap ChannelMap_CP_4_site ^
  -b "Base.igxl" --cslibrarypath "C:\Library\bin" -o "Output" --job CP1 --charplan "CharPlan.xlsx"

TagDiff

Compares an autogen-produced test program against a production reference test program, sheet by sheet, and writes an Excel automation-rate report plus per-sheet KDiff3-ready diff artifacts. 

AutogenCommandLine.exe -e TagDiff -a "Glennie.igxl" -p "UR89_CP1_PROD.igxl" -o "Output" --job CP1

How to Use

Prepare InputsAutogen output program plus the matching production reference program
➜
Run CommandCall with -e TagDiff after an Autogen run completes
➜
Check OutputOpen _AutoRate_*.xlsx: Pivot/Data sheets for rate, per-sheet tabs for diffs
FlagRequiredDescription
-a, --autogen-tpYesPath to the autogen test program (.igxl or .xls).
-p, --prod-tpYesPath to the production reference test program (.igxl or .xls).
-o, --out-dirYesOutput directory for the report and exported sheets.
-j, --jobNoJob name used when comparing job-list sheets.
-c, --only-csharpNoSwitch flag — only compare C# instance sheets.
--exclude_dirsNoComma-separated list of directory paths. Each path must exist; every file found in it (recursively) contributes its filename — without extension — as a sheet name to mark Exclude in the Data sheet and drop from the Pivot sheet totals.
-m, --mockNo0/1 — mock mode.

TagDiff Report Output

Running -e TagDiff writes <AutogenTpName>_AutoRate_<timestamp>.xlsx to the output directory, alongside Autogen\ / Production\ exported-sheet folders and a Diff\ folder of KDiff3 batch files (when the OASISROOT environment variable is set). The report below was generated from the repository's own Glennie regression fixtures (TagDiff\TagDiff.Test\Input\Glennie) via AutogenCommandLine.exe -e TagDiff -a Glennie.igxl -p UR89_CP1_..._PROD....igxl -o Output --job CP1 -m 1.

Legend Sheet

Explains the color coding used throughout the Data sheet and every per-sheet detail tab: green = identical, yellow = different (shown as ReferenceValue => AutogenValue), red = present in the reference program only, grey = present in the autogen program only, and no color means the row/cell was not exercised by the comparison. Output_hashes, ExecInfo, and Versions sheets are always excluded from the summary.

Pivot Sheet

A rollup pivot of automation rate by category (Basic, DC, ATPG, Efuse, RTOS, BinCut, CZ, Other under "non-Hip"; HardIP and RegAssign under "Hip"), with pass/fail/total counts and a grand total row.

Data Sheet

One row per compared IGXL sheet, grouped by category/block, with the automation rate split into T-AutoGen / Manual / Semi-automated percentages, item counts, and a hyperlink in the Link column that jumps straight to that sheet's detail tab.

Per-Sheet Detail Tab

Each compared sheet (for example Flow_Rtos_UART, shown below) gets its own tab with a row-by-row Status column (P = pass, MissingBase / MissingCompare = present on only one side), the base/compared file and row numbers, and the full set of flow/instance columns (Opcode, Parameter, TName, TNum, LoLim, HiLim, Scale, Units, Format, …) so a mismatch can be traced back to the exact row.

Text Report

A plain-text file (OverView TXT) is generated alongside the Excel report, derived from the Pivot sheet — useful for quick reviews or feeding the automation rate into other tools without opening Excel.

JSON Report

A JSON file is also generated, storing the elapsed time for each processing block of the comparison run.

Metrics Reference

MetricDescriptionFormula
AutoGenRatePercentage of automatically generated items((Total - Manual - SemiAuto) / Total) x 100
ManualCountItems not found in the reference program—
SemiAutoCountItems found but mismatched—
FailCountTotal failed itemsManualCount + SemiAutoCount

BenchLog

BenchLogOptions defines a large option set for bench-log-driven pattern/program generation (PinMap, EfuseBitDefition, BenchLog folder, register map, etc.), and -e BenchLog does resolve to that options class in CommandLineFactory.GetOptions. However, CommandLineFactory.GetSubCommandLineApplication has no BenchLogOptions branch, so the dispatcher currently falls through to the generic AutogenCommandLineApp handler, which expects AutogenOptions. Treat this entry as reserved/in-progress rather than a supported CLI path today.

How to Use

Not usable yet — do not run -e BenchLog.

6. Tips

  • Always quote file/folder paths that contain spaces — every entry's help text calls this out explicitly.
  • Use -m 1 when trying out a command interactively: it freezes timestamps and mocks the assembly version, so repeated runs produce identically-named output files instead of a new timestamped file each time.
  • For Autogen/Validation, prefer --repo over hand-listing every config flag — most Settings\... paths are resolved automatically from the repo folder and current project name via AutogenOptions.Initialize().
  • For a quick end-to-end sanity check of the whole pipeline (test plan → program → TagDiff automation rate), run -e Autogen against a known test plan, then feed the resulting program into -e TagDiff against a production reference for the same job.
  • For TagDiff, use -c / --only-csharp when you only care about C# instance sheets — this significantly reduces run time. Use --exclude_dirs to keep known-noisy sheets out of the Pivot totals: put a file named after each sheet (e.g. rtos_configuration.txt) into a folder and pass that folder's path; matching rows are still listed on the Data sheet but flagged Exclude.
  • Because argument parsing ignores unknown flags, a copy-pasted command line for the wrong entry will not error loudly — double-check -e before trusting a "no errors" run.
